name: Cursa
description: A star 27 parsecs away, 3.4 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 23875: radius 3.439 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 43.469 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.035) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 23875: effective temperature 7997 +/- 144 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.028)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 23875: distance 27.397 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.012), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 27 parsecs away, 3.4 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 43 times the Sun's luminosity at 7,997 K, so 3.439 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 23875: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Beta Eridani
quotes.card: Beta Eridani, formally named Cursa, is the second-brightest star in the barely equatorial-southern constellation of Eridanus, located in the northeast end of this constellation near the shared border with Orion.
quotes.introduction: The apparent visual magnitude of this star is 2.796, so it can be viewed with the naked eye in dark skies.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 3211922645854328832 (quality A), from 2006AstL...32..759G; Gaia DR3 measures none
